subject: General Awareness
summary: Current affairs questions in DSSSB ask about schemes, international organisations, sports events, awards, science missions and reports/indices, usually from the 12-18 months before the exam. These notes give a preparation method plus the stable background facts (headquarters, report publishers, important days, sports trophies and terms) that recur every year; any recent event, rank or winner must be checked in a current source before the exam.

subject: General Awareness
summary: Indian history from the Harappan civilisation through the Vedic age, Buddhism and Jainism, the Mauryas and Guptas, the Delhi Sultanate and Mughals, to British rule and the freedom struggle, plus authors of classical and modern works. DSSSB asks one-line factual questions (years of battles and movements, founders, places) and 'which pair is correct' items, so chronology and pairing matter most.

subject: General Awareness
summary: The making and features of the Indian Constitution, the most-asked articles, schedules and amendments, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Fundamental Duties, the Union executive and Parliament, the judiciary and constitutional bodies, and Panchayati Raj and municipalities (with Delhi's special status). DSSSB regularly asks 'which article deals with...' and article/schedule pair questions, so the article map is the core of this note.

subject: General Awareness
summary: India's location, physiographic divisions, mountain ranges, rivers and lakes, monsoon climate and natural phenomena (earthquake waves, winds, atmosphere, rocks), key world geography facts, and soils, forests, crops and minerals. DSSSB asks direct facts (origin of a river, tributary pairs, hill ranges) and 'which statement is correct' items, plus small calculations such as time difference from longitude.

subject: General Awareness
summary: Money and its measures, banking and the RBI's monetary policy tools, the Union Budget, deficits and taxation, national income concepts and other basic economic ideas, and the main economic institutions in India and abroad. DSSSB questions follow NCERT macroeconomics language closely (money multiplier, high-powered money, intermediate goods, disposable income in a recession), so precise definitions earn the marks.

subject: General Awareness
summary: NCERT-level physics, chemistry and biology as they appear in daily life: mirrors and lenses, refraction and sound, friction and electricity; acids, bases, common compounds and separation methods; cells, blood, vitamins, diseases and enzymes; and ecology and environmental protection. DSSSB asks short factual questions (which acid is in orange, image position in a concave mirror, organism causing wheat rust), so clear tables and a few key formulas cover most of the marks.

subject: General Awareness
summary: Indian music and the classical classification of instruments, classical and folk dances and theatre forms, state festivals, fairs and monuments, national and international awards, and well-known books and their authors. DSSSB repeatedly asks instrument-type pairs (tata, sushira, avanaddha, ghana), dance-state and festival-state pairs, 'which monument is in which state' and author-book matches.

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
summary: Analogy (A : B :: C : ?) and classification (odd one out) with words, letters, letter clusters, numbers and number pairs. These are the quickest marks in the reasoning section if you know the common word relationships, the alphabet position values and the standard number patterns (squares, cubes, primes, n² ± n).

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
summary: Number series, letter and alphanumeric series, and missing/wrong-term questions. DSSSB papers carry several series questions every year, including 'one term is wrong' items and letter-cluster series where each position follows its own rule. A fixed checking order (differences, ratios, squares/cubes, alternation, position-wise letters) solves almost all of them within a minute.

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
summary: Letter coding (shifts, opposites, reversals, rearrangements), number coding (position values, sums and products), sentence/word coding, and symbol or mathematical-operation substitution including sign interchange. DSSSB sets 2-4 such questions per paper; each falls to a short checklist of transformations followed by careful BODMAS arithmetic.

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
summary: Blood relations (pointing/photograph statements, coded relations, family puzzles) and direction sense (turns, rotations through angles, shortest distance, shadows and direction-mapping). Both are solved reliably by drawing: a family tree with fixed symbols, or a path on a compass grid with Pythagoras for the final distance.

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
summary: Linear and circular seating arrangements, ranking and position in a row, comparison (inequality) puzzles, and calendar and clock problems. DSSSB sets several of these every year; the keys are a disciplined diagram for seating, two simple formulas for ranking, the odd-days method for calendars and the 30H − 5.5M formula for clock angles.

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
summary: Syllogisms (definite and possibility conclusions, either-or cases), statement and arguments, statement and assumptions or conclusions, cause and effect, courses of action, and assertion-reason. DSSSB papers include several of these each year; they reward strict reading: accept only what the statement guarantees, and judge arguments and actions by fixed criteria rather than personal opinion.

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
summary: Venn diagrams (choosing the diagram for a set of classes and reading numbers from a given diagram), non-verbal figure questions (mirror and water images, paper folding, embedded figures, figure series and analogies, dice and cubes), and counting figures (triangles, squares, rectangles). Several DSSSB questions each year come from these, and most are solved by a few rules plus systematic counting.

subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
summary: Covers the types of numbers, divisibility rules, factors, unit digits and remainders, HCF and LCM (including word problems), BODMAS simplification, indices and surds, and fractions and recurring decimals. DSSSB asks several quick numerical questions in this area in every paper (simplify an expression, find HCF/LCM, compare surds, convert a decimal), so speed with rules and shortcuts matters more than long working.

subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
summary: Covers percentage basics and fraction equivalents, percentage change and successive change, expenditure and population problems, profit and loss, marked price and discounts, and simple and compound interest. These are the most frequent arithmetic questions in DSSSB papers; almost all of them reduce to multiplying factors such as 1.2 or 0.85, so fraction-percent equivalents and the successive-change formula save a lot of time.

subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
summary: Covers ratio and proportion, averages (including replacement, inclusion and average speed), problems on ages, alligation and mixtures, and partnership. These topics share one idea, expressing quantities as multiples of a common unit, and DSSSB regularly asks one or two direct questions from each, which can be solved in under a minute with the unit method and the alligation rule.

subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
summary: Covers time and work (LCM/efficiency method, group work, man-days), pipes and cisterns, speed-time-distance with unit conversion and relative speed, late/early and meeting problems, trains, and boats and streams. DSSSB papers usually contain two or three of these questions; the LCM method for work and the relative-speed idea for trains cover most of them.

subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
summary: Covers areas and perimeters of plane figures, volumes and surface areas of solids (including melting and recasting), and the geometry of lines, polygons, triangles and circles. DSSSB asks direct formula-based questions here (area of a triangle or circle, volume of a sphere or cone, revolutions of a wheel, angles in a circle), so an accurate formula sheet and the standard theorems are enough for most marks.

subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
summary: Covers algebraic identities and their standard applications (x + 1/x, a + b + c = 0), linear and quadratic equations, trigonometric ratios and identities, heights and distances, data interpretation from tables, bar, line and pie charts, and basic statistics (mean, median, mode). DSSSB includes identity-based value questions and a data-interpretation set in most papers; both reward knowing the shortcut forms rather than full expansion.

subject: Hindi Language
subtopics: अनेक शब्दों के लिए एक शब्द
summary: इस अध्याय में पर्यायवाची, अनेकार्थी, विलोम, अनेक शब्दों के लिए एक शब्द, तत्सम-तद्भव-देशज-विदेशज शब्द और श्रुतिसम-भिन्नार्थक युग्म शब्द शामिल हैं। DSSSB के हिंदी खंड में हर प्रश्नपत्र में इनसे कई सीधे प्रश्न आते हैं, जो शब्द याद होने पर कुछ ही सेकंड में हल हो जाते हैं; इसलिए मानक सूचियों का नियमित अभ्यास सबसे अधिक लाभ देता है।

subject: Hindi Language
summary: इस अध्याय में संधि (स्वर, व्यंजन, विसर्ग), समास के छह भेद, संज्ञा-सर्वनाम-विशेषण, क्रिया-काल-वाच्य, कारक और अव्यय, उपसर्ग-प्रत्यय तथा लिंग-वचन के नियम उदाहरण सहित दिए गए हैं। DSSSB के हिंदी खंड में संधि-विच्छेद, समास-विग्रह, कारक और लिंग-वचन से हर बार सीधे प्रश्न आते हैं; नियम और मानक उदाहरण याद हों तो ये अंक पक्के हो जाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Language
summary: इस अध्याय में वर्तनी (मात्रा, संयुक्ताक्षर, अनुस्वार-अनुनासिक, श-ष-स, ण-न) की सामान्य अशुद्धियाँ, वाक्य शुद्धि के नियम (लिंग-वचन-अन्विति, 'ने' का प्रयोग, कारक-चिह्न, पुनरुक्ति, शब्द-क्रम) और विराम चिह्नों के नाम व प्रयोग दिए गए हैं। DSSSB में शुद्ध वर्तनी, शुद्ध वाक्य और उपयुक्त विराम चिह्न के प्रश्न लगभग हर पाली में आते हैं।

subject: Hindi Language
summary: इस अध्याय में मुहावरे और लोकोक्ति की परिभाषा, दोनों में अंतर, शरीर के अंगों और अन्य विषयों से जुड़े प्रचलित मुहावरे, प्रमुख लोकोक्तियाँ तथा इनके प्रश्नों को हल करने की विधि दी गई है। DSSSB के हिंदी खंड में प्रायः हर पाली में एक-दो प्रश्न मुहावरे और लोकोक्ति के अर्थ, रिक्त स्थान या शुद्ध रूप पर आते हैं।

subject: Hindi Language
summary: इस अध्याय में अपठित गद्यांश पढ़ने और उसके प्रश्न (शीर्षक, तथ्य, निष्कर्ष, शब्दार्थ) हल करने की विधि, वाक्यों और वाक्यांशों को सही क्रम में लगाने के संकेत, रचना और अर्थ के आधार पर वाक्य-भेद, तथा रिक्त स्थान पूर्ति की विधि दी गई है। DSSSB के हिंदी खंड में हर पाली में एक गद्यांश पर चार-पाँच प्रश्न, वाक्य क्रम और रिक्त स्थान के प्रश्न आते हैं।

subject: English Language
summary: Covers synonyms, antonyms, one-word substitutions, spelling rules and commonly misspelt words, and idioms, phrases and phrasal verbs, with word roots to decode unfamiliar words. DSSSB English sections ask several direct vocabulary questions per paper; they are answered in seconds if you know the word, so regular revision of high-frequency lists and elimination tricks is the best preparation.

subject: English Language
summary: Covers the grammar rules behind error spotting, sentence improvement and fill-in-the-blank questions: subject-verb agreement, pronouns, adjectives, adverbs and conjunctions, tenses, articles, prepositions, question tags, and the transformation rules for active-passive voice and direct-indirect speech. These rules decide a large share of the English marks in DSSSB papers, and each question usually tests exactly one of them.

subject: English Language
summary: Covers reading comprehension (question types such as title, main idea, inference, tone and word meaning, and the traps in options), para jumbles and sentence-part rearrangement, and cloze tests. DSSSB English sections regularly include a passage with several questions, a few rearrangement questions and a cloze passage; these are reasoning-with-language questions where a clear method beats a large vocabulary.

subject: Computer Science
topicHi: कंप्यूटर मूल सिद्धांत एवं पीसी सॉफ्टवेयर
titleHi: कंप्यूटर मूल सिद्धांत एवं पीसी सॉफ्टवेयर
summary: Covers the history and generations of computers, classification, input/output hardware, memory and storage units, types of software and utilities, MS Office/LibreOffice usage with keyboard shortcuts, and Internet and e-mail basics. DSSSB asks several direct one-liners from this area every paper (full forms, which generation used what, impact vs non-impact printers, OMR/MICR, time and storage units), so these are quick, high-scoring marks.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Covers positional number systems and base conversions, complements and binary arithmetic, binary codes (BCD, Excess-3, Gray, ASCII, Unicode), Boolean algebra and logic gates, K-map minimisation, combinational circuits (adders, multiplexers, decoders) and sequential circuits (flip-flops, registers, counters). DSSSB papers regularly ask numerical conversions, K-map simplifications, gate counts and MUX/counter formulas, so accurate, fast working is essential.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Covers CPU organisation (ALU, control unit, registers), micro-operations and the instruction cycle, instruction formats and addressing modes, the memory hierarchy, memory sizing and cache mapping, pipelining and Flynn's classification, I/O transfer modes with interrupts and DMA, and assembly language basics. DSSSB questions here follow Morris Mano closely: register names, addressing-mode definitions, address/data line counts, DMA modes and pseudo-instructions are asked almost every year.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Covers C from data types, operators and expressions through control statements, functions and recursion, arrays and strings, pointers and dynamic memory, structures, unions and file handling, to the preprocessor and the compilation process. DSSSB regularly asks output-prediction questions (octal/hex constants, % with negatives, ++/--, comma operator, integer division), identifier and keyword rules, and array address calculations, so every rule here is backed by code with its exact output.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Object-oriented concepts and how C++ and Java implement them: classes, constructors, inheritance, overloading, virtual functions, templates and exceptions, plus Java's JVM, data types, packages, interfaces and threads. DSSSB asks many statement-based and output-tracing questions here, so exact rules and outputs matter.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Python syntax, data types, operators, control flow, strings, lists, tuples, sets, dictionaries, functions, modules and file handling, with exact outputs of typical code. DSSSB asks direct questions on built-in functions, methods and file modes, and output-prediction questions, so the precise behaviour of each feature matters.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Arrays, stacks, queues, linked lists, trees (binary trees, BST, AVL, heaps, B-trees), graphs, hashing, searching and sorting, with their complexities. This is one of the most heavily tested areas in DSSSB TGT Computer Science: expect traversal, BST/heap construction, hashing, sorting-pass and complexity questions.

subject: Computer Science
summary: How algorithms are represented (pseudocode, flowcharts) and analysed (asymptotic notation, loop counting, recurrences, Master theorem), the main design paradigms (divide and conquer, greedy, dynamic programming) and the standard graph algorithms (BFS, DFS, MST, shortest paths). DSSSB regularly asks complexity values, flowchart symbols and short traces of these algorithms.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Covers OS types and functions, processes and threads, CPU scheduling, synchronisation and deadlock, memory management and virtual memory, file systems, disk scheduling and everyday Linux commands. DSSSB papers ask both direct definition questions (spooling, dispatcher, thrashing, Belady's anomaly, /etc) and short numericals on page faults, scheduling and deadlock-free resource counts.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Covers database concepts and the three-schema architecture, the ER model and keys, the relational model and relational algebra, SQL (DDL, DML, joins, aggregates), functional dependencies and normal forms, and transactions with concurrency control and recovery. DSSSB papers ask many one-line factual questions (keys, Codd's rules, SQL operators and functions, checkpoint, timestamp) along with short query-output and normal-form problems.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Covers network types and topologies, switching, the OSI and TCP/IP models, transmission media and connecting devices, data-link framing, error and flow control and medium access, IPv4/IPv6 addressing with subnetting and routing, and the main transport and application protocols with their ports. DSSSB asks layer-function, device-layer, protocol full-form and port questions, plus small calculations on subnets, CRC, Hamming code and channel capacity.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Covers security goals and attacks, malware types, symmetric and public-key cryptography (DES, AES, RSA, Diffie–Hellman), hashing, digital signatures and certificates, firewalls, authentication and secure protocols, and Indian cyber law under the IT Act, 2000 with its 2008 amendment. DSSSB questions test definitions (worm vs virus vs Trojan, firewall types, SSL, digital certificates) and the main IT Act sections and penalties.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Covers how the web works (HTTP, URLs, servers, hosting), HTML and HTML5, CSS selectors and layout, JavaScript with the DOM event model, XML with DTD/Schema and parsers, front-end tools and the Microsoft .NET/ASP.NET platform. DSSSB asks many one-line fact questions here: tag attributes, CSS property names, event names, XML rules and .NET full forms.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Covers the software life cycle and process models (waterfall, prototype, incremental, RAD, spiral, agile), requirements and SRS, design quality (cohesion, coupling, partitioning), testing techniques and cyclomatic complexity, estimation (FP, COCOMO, PERT/CPM) and maintenance, quality and reliability. DSSSB regularly asks model names, cohesion/coupling definitions, testing terms, full forms (CASE, SQA, MTTF, ROCOF) and formula-based questions.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Covers display hardware (CRT, raster/random scan, flat panels, colour models), line and circle algorithms (DDA, Bresenham, midpoint), 2D/3D transformations and projections, clipping (Cohen-Sutherland, Liang-Barsky, Sutherland-Hodgman), curves, hidden-surface removal and shading, and multimedia digitisation, compression and file formats. Exams mix definition questions (CRT parts, resolution, emissive displays, formats) with short numericals on algorithms, transformations and colour conversion.

subject: Computer Science
topicHi: ई-कॉमर्स, MIS एवं व्यवसाय में IT
titleHi: ई-कॉमर्स, MIS एवं व्यवसाय में IT
summary: Covers e-commerce types, business and revenue models, electronic payment systems, security and EDI; information systems for management (TPS, MIS, DSS, ESS, expert systems, data warehousing and OLAP); knowledge management; and ERP with related business systems such as CRM, SCM and accounting software. DSSSB questions are mostly conceptual: model classification, payment-system features, system components and types of knowledge.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Covers mobile computing and its limitations, cellular generations and GSM architecture, wireless LAN/Bluetooth/MANET and mobility, cloud computing (characteristics, IaaS/PaaS/SaaS, deployment, virtualisation), AI and machine learning basics, IoT, and other emerging technologies such as big data, blockchain, AR/VR and quantum computing. DSSSB asks full forms (GSM, GPRS), generation and speed ordering, cloud features, ML types and IoT challenges.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Covers cyber ethics, cyber crime and India's IT Act, AI ethics (bias, black boxes, deepfakes), intellectual property rights and software licences, e-waste hazards and the E-Waste (Management) Rules, and digital footprints, privacy and the DPDP Act, 2023. Questions are factual and scenario based: which right or section applies, which substance is hazardous, what counts as a child or a passive footprint.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Covers sets, relations, functions and propositional logic; matrices, determinants and basic calculus; probability with Bayes' theorem; random variables, binomial/Poisson/normal distributions and descriptive statistics with regression; and numerical methods - interpolation, root finding and numerical integration. DSSSB asks short numericals here (Bayes, median, variance, Lagrange/Newton interpolation, determinants), so know the formulas and practise the calculations.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Covers business communication and forms of business organisation, the fundamentals of financial accounting (concepts, rules of debit and credit, books, trial balance, depreciation, BRS, bills of exchange), and business economics (demand, elasticity, costs, market structures and RBI monetary policy). These small units give easy marks in DSSSB through direct definition and short calculation questions.

subject: Computer Science
summary: Covers SI units, electric charge and Coulomb's law, current and resistance, series and parallel circuits, power and AC basics, elasticity and fluid flow, and semiconductors - band theory, doping, p-n junction diodes, rectifiers and transistors. DSSSB asks direct questions here (laws, units, equivalent resistance, moduli, types of flow, transistor facts), so a quick formula revision earns easy marks.

subject: Teaching Methodology
summary: Covers how children learn and how teachers teach: behaviourist, cognitive and constructivist theories (Pavlov, Thorndike, Skinner, Piaget, Vygotsky, Bruner, Bandura), teaching approaches, methods and maxims, motivation theories, and Bloom's taxonomy with writing of instructional objectives. Theory–thinker matching, Piaget's stage ages and Bloom's levels are among the most frequently asked pedagogy questions.

subject: Teaching Methodology
summary: Covers how children grow and develop: principles and stages of development, heredity and environment, Erikson's psychosocial and Kohlberg's moral stages, socialisation and play, intelligence (IQ, theories, intellectual disability ranges), individual differences and creativity, and the needs of adolescents. Stage ages, theorist–theory matching and IQ calculations are regular exam questions.

subject: Teaching Methodology
summary: Covers the pedagogy of Computer Science (PCK, computational thinking, CS-specific methods such as pair programming, PRIMM and unplugged activities, and common programming misconceptions), learning resources and ICT (Dale's Cone, diorama/realia, e-learning, SAMR, Indian digital platforms), and lesson planning (Herbart, 5E, Gagné, microteaching). These link directly to classroom-practice questions in the Teaching Methodology section.

subject: Teaching Methodology
summary: Covers assessment concepts (measurement vs evaluation; assessment of, for and as learning), formative, summative, diagnostic and placement assessment, CCE under the RTE Act and NEP 2020 reforms, test items and item analysis, qualities of a good test, and evaluation tools such as rubrics, portfolios, checklists and anecdotal records. Questions on formative assessment features, peer assessment and item types appear regularly.

subject: Teaching Methodology
summary: Covers the move from exclusion to inclusion, models of disability, who children with special needs are, the RPwD Act 2016 and its 21 disabilities, learning disabilities and support for sensory, intellectual and developmental disabilities, inclusive practices (UDL, differentiation, IEP), Indian policies and schemes, and accessible computing in the CS lab. Expect questions on Act provisions, disability types and classroom strategies.

subject: Teaching Methodology
summary: Covers knowledge and curriculum concepts (types of knowledge, curriculum vs syllabus, hidden curriculum, Tyler's model, philosophical foundations), NCF 2005 and NCF 2022–23, the RTE Act 2009 with its key sections and Schedule norms, national policies (1968, 1986/1992, NEP 2020), schemes such as SSA and Samagra Shiksha, and the chronology of education commissions. Policy years, Act sections and commission names are high-frequency factual questions.

subject: Teaching Methodology
summary: Covers sex and gender, gender socialisation and bias in schools, equality vs equity, constitutional and legal provisions on gender, policies for girls' education, and the relation between school and society including agencies of education and school–family–community partnerships. Questions test definitions, policy years and practical classroom responses.

subject: Teaching Methodology
summary: Covers the idea that every teacher is a language teacher: language and thought (Piaget, Vygotsky, Chomsky, Skinner, Krashen), Cummins' BICS and CALP, subject-specific vocabulary, home language and multilingualism in policy (NCF 2005, NEP 2020, Article 350A, Eighth Schedule), and practical reading, writing and talk strategies, including in the Computer Science classroom. A small but regular source of one-mark questions.

subject: Teaching Methodology
summary: Covers art education (visual and performing arts), NCF 2005 and NEP 2020 positions, children's artistic development, regional and folk art forms, art-integrated learning with Computer Science examples, and drama in education – its pioneers, techniques such as role-play, hot-seating and forum theatre, and the teacher's role. Questions usually test definitions and the purpose of art and drama in learning.
